kjv: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth
mine: For there are three that testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood
note: The "Johannine Comma" (5:7b–8a) appears in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century (and then only in a few late ones, some with the words added in the margin), in no early version, and in no Greek Father during the Trinitarian controversies; it arose in Latin commentary and entered the Vulgate tradition. Erasmus added it to his third edition (1522) after a recently copied Greek manuscript containing it (minuscule 61) was produced. It is the only explicit Trinitarian formula in the KJV NT and has no claim to be original. Spans 5:7–8. Context: three that testify: the Spirit, the water and the blood (no Comma) (high confidence). The heavenly witnesses appear in no Greek manuscript before about the 14th century (629, 61, 918, 2318 and a few margins), in no early version, and in no Greek Father during the Trinitarian debates; they arose in Latin sources (Priscillian, c. 380) and entered later Vulgate copies. 5:6 and 5:8 carry the Spirit-water-blood argument. Other possible meanings: (1) 'three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one' — TR (Erasmus 1522 onward), KJV, later Vulgate manuscripts, perhaps Cyprian (De unitate 6); the Byzantine Majority Text lacks it; (2) the Spirit, water and blood read as baptism, the cross and the eucharist — an interpretation of the shorter text.
